title: Pip's Lost Blanket
markdown:
Once upon a time, in the warmest sunniest spot of Lanternwood, lived a kind wizard named Otis Pine. His beard was soft like fluffy dandelions. His magic made gentle shimmery sparks, like tiny fireflies blinking hello. Otis loved to make his soft sparks dance, especially when his puffin friend, Pip, was near. Pip was a puffin as round and fluffy as a little cloud. Pip’s very favourite thing in the whole wide world was his fuzzy blue blanket. Blue like a clear sky. Soft as a whispered secret.

Every day was a happy calm day in Lanternwood. Otis would make his sparks go flicker, flicker, glow. Pip would waddle beside him. Little feet, pitter-patter on the moss. Then, when it was time for a little rest, Pip would find his special spot. He would snuggle down deep, deep, deep into his fuzzy blue blanket. He would let out the happiest little chirp, a sound full of cozy warmth.

Until one day, something strange happened. Pip waddled to his cozy spot, ready to snuggle. But his fuzzy blue blanket was gone. Pip looked left. Pip looked right. He tilted his head. His eyes were big and round. The spot where his blanket should be was all empty.

“Oh dear, oh dear,” chirped Pip. His little wings drooped. A funny wiggle in his tummy.

Otis, with his kind wizard ears, heard the worried chirp. He trotted over.

“What’s wrong, Pip?” His voice as soft as a bedtime story.

Pip pointed a little flipper at the empty spot.

“My blanket.” A wobble in the peep.

“Don’t worry, Pip.” Otis put a kind hand on Pip’s feathery head. Warm. Steady. “We will find it. Let’s go on an adventure to the Pebblecloud Peaks. Sometimes things like to play peek-a-boo there.”

Because of that, Otis Pine and Pip set off. The path was lined with soft green moss. Pretty pebbles lay everywhere, and when they walked the pebbles made a sound like tiny happy bells. As they climbed higher the air grew warmer. Soon they saw the soft glow of many lanterns, peeking through fluffy white mist, like a field of sleepy stars.

As they turned a gentle corner, they met Glimmerwick. Glimmerwick was a goblin, but not a grumpy one. Glimmerwick was a lantern-keeper. His happy job was to make sure all the lanterns shone bright and warm. He was polishing a big lantern that glowed like a cheerful golden sun.

“Hello there, travellers,” he chirped, voice like little bells. “Did you lose something?”

“Yes, please,” chirped Pip, waddling closer, fluffy tail giving a hopeful little wag. “My fuzzy blue blanket is gone. It’s my very favourite.”

“A missing blanket is a very important thing to find,” said Glimmerwick, eyes twinkling. “I have not seen a fuzzy blue blanket. But I have seen many curious things float by on the breezes up here. Come with me, and I will help you look near my lanterns.”

Because of that, Glimmerwick led Otis and Pip deeper among the softly shining lanterns. They hung from twisty vines. Some were shaped like happy stars. Others were like sleepy moons. They smelled sweet, like warm honey and gentle sunshine. Glimmerwick pointed with a little goblin finger.

“Did it float this way? Or maybe it snuggled near that big lantern over there?”

Pip waddled with all his might. Otis looked with his keen wizard eyes. Still no fuzzy blue blanket.

Otis remembered his own magic. He wiggled his fingers. Soft shimmery sparks flew out, flicker, flicker, glow. They danced around the lanterns and made the light even prettier. They did not show the blanket. Otis let out a tiny quiet wizard sigh.

Then Pip, who had been looking down, looked up. Way, way up. He pointed a little flipper toward the very top of the tallest lantern. Caught gently on a wisp of a puffy cloud: something fuzzy and blue. His blanket. It must have floated up with a playful gust of wind when he wasn’t looking.

“My blanket,” Pip chirped. His whole fluffy body wiggled.

But how could they get it down? Too high for Pip. Otis’s sparks were lovely, but not strong enough to pull. Glimmerwick wriggled his pointy ears and hummed a thoughtful sound. Otis looked at Pip, then at the blanket so high up. A wonderful idea sparked. He gathered his shimmery sparks, just enough to make a gentle warm light. He aimed them very carefully. Not to pull. To nudge. Flicker, flicker, nudge. A stream of soft warm sparks to the cloud. The cloud gave a little wiggle. Then it began to drift. The fuzzy blue blanket floated down, down, down.

Until finally, with a soft feathery whoosh, the fuzzy blue blanket landed right at Pip’s happy little feet. Pip gave a joyful chirp. He snuggled into its familiar comfort at once. Wiggled his little toes. Felt the wonderful fuzzy feeling all around him. A deep happy sigh. His feathery chest puffed. Otis smiled. Glimmerwick clapped his little goblin hands.

“Hooray,” he giggled.

Ever since then, Pip always made sure his fuzzy blue blanket was tucked extra, extra close. Otis Pine and Pip enjoyed many more cozy evenings in Lanternwood, filled with soft sparks, happy chirps, and the warm hug of a fuzzy blue blanket. The lanterns kept their honey smell. The pebbles kept their tiny bells. Pip kept the blanket, and the blanket, at last, kept Pip.
characters: Otis Pine (kind wizard), Pip (puffin), Glimmerwick (goblin lantern-keeper)
